effective_date_basis: Effective date of the revoking instrument per tract, or a current basis.
ending_pattern: A withdrawal continues until revoked or modified, or, for a tract, until it is patented or sold (townsite and cemetery withdrawals). Temporary withdrawals 'pending resurvey' or 'for classification' end when the purpose is completed and the order is revoked; the revoking instrument, not the purpose, usually supplies the exact date. Restoration orders end parts of earlier withdrawals.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Valid existing rights. FLPMA (Pub. L. 94-579, Oct. 21, 1976) s.704(a) repealed the Pickett Act and implied withdrawal authority prospectively; s.701 saves existing withdrawals until modified under FLPMA or other law (IBLA, Grant L. Hacking, 1980). This is a continuity point, never an end; the s.204(l) review of withdrawals is a review lead, not an end.

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.
The order itself revokes or modifies another order (its lifecycle is spent on issue, and it is evidence for the other order's end).

Overlapping later blanket withdrawals (for example the 1934-35 general withdrawals pending Taylor Grazing Act classification, EO 6910 and EO 6964): a revocation of the earlier order may leave the land withdrawn under the later one.
Alaska lands affected by ANCSA, statehood selections and the Alaska Lands Act.

Stock driveways (the separate stock-driveway rule was withdrawn for lack of a held exemplar): withdrawn under s.10 of the Stock-Raising Homestead Act of 1916 (39 Stat. 862); apply this rule with that authority.
quoted_clause: Under the provisions of the act approved June 25, 1910 (36 Stat., 847), authorizing the President of the United States to make withdrawals of public lands in certain cases, it is hereby ordered that the public lands specifically described as the southwest quarter of the northeast quarter, the southeast quarter, the east half and the southwest quarter of the southwest quarter, section thirty-five, township seven south, range three east of the Black Hills Meridian, South Dakota, be and the same are hereby temporarily withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, or entry. The purpose of this withdrawal is to permit such examination of the lands as may be necessary to determine their availability for a permanent reservation under the provisions of the national monument act, approved June 8, 1906 (34 Stat., 225), to protect, in the public interest, the rich mesozoic deposits of cycads and other characteristic examples of paleobotany numerously found there.

The purpose of this withdrawal is to permit such examination of the lands as may be necessary to determine their availability for a permanent reservation under the provisions of the national monument act, approved June 8, 1906 (34 Stat., 225), to protect, in the public interest, the rich mesozoic deposits of cycads and other characteristic examples of paleobotany numerously found there.
required_evidence: The order's text with the lands.
Later revocations or PLOs (X2) naming the order by date or number.

scope.note: Membership is a machine lead; each order is decided by an agent, row by row.

source.custody_limit: Exemplar text is a held copy graded mirror_transcription; it illustrates the type's wording and is not an authenticated original.
